claims.title: Nominal all-word equivalence
claims.statement: For every n>=2, route pair (a,b) and finite target word, setting all source values to each target yields correct action and prediction with zero discrepancy at every step; an appended calibrated R204 row-replacement predictor retains the same forward-state trace.
scope: pure fixed routes with a calibrated identity plant/predictor
all_of: nominal sources yoked to target
R204 update law for forward-state clause
limits: Nominal equality is not equality under arbitrary diagnostic probes.
Actual writes can differ while register states match.

claims.title: Exact source-observation fibers
claims.statement: For schedule W with source columns c_i, full consumer readouts yield product fibers of equal columns; mismatch-only observation yields {(i,j):c_i XOR c_j=d}. Under a restricted intervention family sources equivalent on every admissible input remain indistinguishable.
scope: finite source sites and pure route consumers
all_of: same declared installation, source carrier sites, consumers, plant and episode/readout binding
independently addressed valid binary source interventions
fixed stated response class and stable route/reset conditions
faithful specified observations; no omitted route, writer, timing or context change
limits: Mismatch-only data generally do not identify an ordered route pair.
A source-code collision is not absence of actual use.

claims.title: Unknown pure-route minimum
claims.statement: For n>=2 unknown pure-route roots, uniform exact decision of their equality using binary source interventions and mismatch-only observations has worst-case minimum ceil(log2 n), including deterministic adaptive protocols.
all_of: same declared installation, source carrier sites, consumers, plant and episode/readout binding
independently addressed valid binary source interventions
fixed stated response class and stable route/reset conditions
faithful specified observations; no omitted route, writer, timing or context change
limits: Does not identify which shared root or local production.

claims.title: Known motor-root minimum
claims.statement: For n>=2 and an independently known motor root a, setting a to zero and all other roots to one decides equality with an unknown predictor root in one probe. It also identifies B={a} for a predictor OR of a nonempty subset B.
all_of: same declared installation, source carrier sites, consumers, plant and episode/readout binding
independently addressed valid binary source interventions
fixed stated response class and stable route/reset conditions
faithful specified observations; no omitted route, writer, timing or context change
known source does not come from the same classification outcome
limits: A report of authorship is not independently known source identity.
Empty constant-zero predictor is outside the OR extension.

claims.title: Redundant OR-set minimum and alias
claims.statement: For n>=2, exact uniform equality decision between arbitrary nonempty OR source subsets requires exactly n probes in the worst case, even adaptively. Along the zero-discrepancy branch each unit input e_i is necessary; all unit inputs suffice. A four-source disjoint-set construction defeats the two-bit pure-route code.
scope: both consumers OR arbitrary nonempty subsets of the n sources
all_of: same declared installation, source carrier sites, consumers, plant and episode/readout binding
independently addressed valid binary source interventions
fixed stated response class and stable route/reset conditions
faithful specified observations; no omitted route, writer, timing or context change
OR response class replaces, rather than inherits, pure-route promise
limits: Target is equality of root sets, not nonempty intersection or intake identity.
No claim that biological prediction implements OR.

claims.title: Source-to-intake resolution boundary
claims.statement: Faithful copy networks with the same composite root-to-consumer map yield identical readouts for all source inputs, while immediate intake carrier identity can differ. A node write and a branch-edge replacement can have distinct cross-consumer effects; only the former separates the displayed shared/separate relay pair under additional targeting premises.
scope: specific shared/separate relay alternative for clamp comparison
all_of: same source input/readout model
faithful copies for factorization result
independently targeted physical carrier for node-write contrast
fixed paths; no intervening overwrite/compensation
limits: Does not recover actual prior-episode occurrence, RetBind or numerical personal identity.
Edge effect does not establish shared carrier occurrence.

claims.title: Prediction chronology counterexample
claims.statement: A postconsequence copy can match all source/readout values of a preconsequence predictor; values alone do not establish the prediction role. The event model distinguishes the implementations by independently recorded chronology.
all_of: same output values
different actual time order
limits: Numerical agreement is not executed prediction or executed comparator evidence.
Timing measurement and interpretation require actual validation.

claims.title: Conditional UCT counterpart and preserved semantic gap
claims.statement: Only under actual-process admission, one complete P/I/K binding, grounded role/trace/time relations, transported physical parameters and C1 do the actual source-consumer relations have experiential structural counterparts. No source confluence, calibration, use, history, language or report threshold is added; H, local membership and conceptual self are not inferred.
scope: one admitted actual process or independently admitted overlapping processes
all_of: A:C1
actual independent physical role grounding
same-instance joint binding
correct formula transport rather than automatic substructure selection
limits: No unique owner or current-assistant consciousness claim.
Complete-organizational twins are not a free phenomenal-difference counterexample inside C1.
